child: Make {member} a cup of tea or hot chocolate and sit with them for 5 minutes.
adult: Make {member} a cup of tea and sit with them for a few minutes. No agenda.

child: Is there something you're sorry about? Write {member} a sorry note that says what happened.
adult: Write {member} a repair note: name what happened, how it may have affected them, and what you'd like to do differently.

child: Give {member} a hug and say 'I'm glad you're my family.'
adult: Tell {member}, in your own words, that you're on their side – even when things are hard between you.

child: Ask {member}: 'Is there anything I did that upset you?' Just listen.
adult: Ask {member}: 'Is there something between us that still feels unfinished?' Listen without defending.

child: Make a 'calm-down plan' with {member}: what helps each of you when you're upset?
adult: Make a cool-down plan with {member}: what will each of you do when an argument starts to heat up?

child: Choose a 'pause' word with {member} to say when an argument gets too loud.
adult: Agree on a 'pause' word with {member} to use when a conversation is getting heated.

child: Ask {member}: 'What can I do to help when you're sad?' Remember the answer!
adult: Ask {member}: 'When you're upset, what helps you most from me?' Write the answer down.

child: Do something kind for {member} – tidy their space, make their bed or share a treat.
adult: Do a quiet act of care for {member} – something that says 'I see you'.

child: Go for a walk with {member} after a hard day. You don't have to talk about it.
adult: After a tense moment, invite {member} for a walk side by side. Let them choose whether to talk.

child: Write {member} a note: 'I'm sorry for… Next time I will try…'
adult: Write {member} a note naming one thing you'd like to do differently after your last disagreement.

child: Tell {member} about a time you disagreed but still loved them.
adult: Tell {member}: 'We don't always agree, and I still love you.' Give an example.

child: Make a 'repair kit' box with {member}: a sorry card, a sweet, a funny photo.
adult: Make a family repair kit with {member}: what helps each of you come back together after a fight?

child: Ask {member} to tell you about a time they felt left out. Just listen and say thank you.
adult: Ask {member} about a time they felt unheard at home. Listen, then say what you understood.

child: Make up after a fight with {member} with a special handshake.
adult: After your next disagreement with {member}, come back within a day and say one thing you understand about their side.

child: Write {member} a note about a time they helped you feel better.
adult: Write {member} about a time they repaired something with you – and what it meant.

child: Ask {member} for a do-over of something that went wrong, and do it nicely this time.
adult: Ask {member} for a 'do-over' of a moment that went badly, and try it again differently.

child: Tell {member} one thing you're going to try to do better, then do it for a day.
adult: Tell {member} one thing you'll work on in how you treat them, then show it for a day.

child: Give {member} a 'calm basket' you made: a stress ball, a soft toy, a nice note.
adult: Put together a small comfort pack for {member} for hard days.

child: Ask {member} to sit with you while you both draw how you feel.
adult: Sit with {member} and each finish this out loud: 'Lately I've been feeling…'

child: Help {member} with something they're finding hard this week.
adult: Notice something {member} is struggling with and offer practical help.
